title: Addressing, Gateways, and DNS
summary: Reason about local addressing, gateways, and name resolution without turning the lesson into certification practice.
objectives: Explain the roles of an IP address and gateway.
Distinguish IP reachability from DNS name resolution.
Use introductory subnet language without requiring subnet mathematics.

vocab.def: A logical address used to identify an interface on a network.
A device or address used to reach another network.
A naming system that resolves a name to an address.

sections.heading: Addressing without overload
sections.body: An address identifies an interface in a network context. A gateway provides a route toward another network. A subnet is a local grouping of addresses; this course uses the concept, not full subnet calculations.

sections.heading: Names and addresses can differ
sections.body: A service can respond when contacted by an IP address while its name fails to resolve. That pattern points toward a DNS investigation, not automatically toward a server failure.

practice.prompt: A synthetic IP check succeeds, but the service name does not resolve. Which system deserves attention first?
practice.answer: Name resolution or DNS evidence deserves attention first because IP connectivity already worked in the scenario.

quiz.question: What does a gateway generally help a host do?

lab.objective: Classify synthetic IP, gateway, and DNS observations.
